body.x: TESOLLO (CEO Young-jin Kim) announced at CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and tech exhibition held in Las Vegas early last month, that it achieved over 20 billion KRW in export consulting value, driven by its independent robot-hand development and optimization technology.

Tesollo is a domestic startup that has developed robotics capabilities, beginning with its multi-joint gripper (robot hand), the DG-3G-B. The company explains that it implements a smaller, more sophisticated structure and precise control performance in its product line compared to existing grippers, leveraging excellent engineering expertise, and is recognized for its unrivaled competitiveness by offering these at reasonable prices.

In particular, the Delto Gripper product line, which represents the company’s capabilities, delivers significantly enhanced precision through a direct-drive design that offers differentiated flexibility, real-time force-control feedback, and AI (Artificial Intelligence)- based software.
Among them, the DG-5F, the latest model and CES entry, received favorable reviews from on-site visitors for demonstrating its ability to perform complex, sophisticated tasks with ease.

This functionality results from integrating high-precision hardware design and AI control software into a single framework. The DG-5F inherits the functionality of the Delto Gripper series, which automatically adjusts gripping force and joint angles in response to factors such as the target object’s size, shape, and surface characteristics.

body.cap: A visitor at CES 2026 examines a demonstration integrating Tesollo’s 5-finger multi-joint robot gripper, Delto Gripper 5F (DG-5F), and the upper-body humanoid robot Adam. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Furthermore, adding the optional tactile sensor significantly enhances interaction capabilities in dynamic environments and enables adaptive force adjustment via slip-detection functions. This provides a task-capability level comparable to that of the human body. Given these advantages, the technology is spreading rapidly across domestic research institutes, and users expect significant utility in physical AI applications such as industrial humanoid robots.

In fact, Tesollo conducted 37 consultations over four days at CES 2026 while showcasing its robot hand product line, including the DG-5F, indicating potential demand of USD 15.18 million (approximately 22.106 billion KRW).

Regarding this, a Tesollo official explained, “We received praise from robotics experts worldwide as we demonstrated our robot hand replicating the minute movements of an operator in real-time at the exhibition site.” They added, “Through this CES, we identified demand for robot gripper technology from various customer groups, and companies in the home appliance and service sectors particularly showed great interest.”

They continued, “The technological references we accumulated by supplying robot hands to major domestic companies and research institutes shone on the global stage, and we expect this achievement to lead to multiple partnerships.” They emphasized, “We will actively utilize the global network secured at CES 2026 to stand tall as a global company representing one axis of the physical AI era.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
